title: Angles
summary: A few angle facts let you find missing angles without measuring. [[angles-at-a-point|Angles at a point]] add up to $360^{\circ}$, angles in [[parallel|parallel]] lines come in equal or supplementary pairs, and a [[polygon|polygon]]'s angles follow from triangles. Each answer needs the value and the fact you used, by name.

goals.text: Find angles at a point, on a straight line and where two lines cross, naming angles with three letters such as angle $ABC$.
Use the [[angle-sum|angle sum]] of a triangle and of a [[quadrilateral|quadrilateral]].
Find angles in parallel lines and give the reason: corresponding, alternate or co-interior.
Find the [[interior-angle|interior angles]] and [[exterior-angle|exterior angles]] of a [[regular-polygon|regular polygon]], or its number of sides.
Find missing angles in any polygon, regular or irregular, from its angle sum or exterior angles.

synonyms: interior and exterior angles of a polygon

before.prompt: An angle is $205^{\circ}$. What type of angle is it?
before.explain: It is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$, so it is reflex. Revise it in {{lesson:4.1}}.

before.prompt: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is it called?
before.hint: Count the pairs of parallel sides each shape has.
before.explain: A trapezium has one pair of parallel sides. A parallelogram and a rhombus have two pairs. Revise it in {{lesson:4.1}}.

sections.heading: Angles at a point and on a line

blocks.text: Angle $ABC$ is the angle at $B$, between the lines $BA$ and $BC$. The middle letter is always the [[vertex|vertex]]. You will also see it written $\angle ABC$.
A full turn is $360^{\circ}$. A straight line is half a turn, $180^{\circ}$.

blocks.alt: Three diagrams. Left: a straight line with a second line leaving it from one point, making two angles a and b with a plus b equal to 180 degrees. Middle: four lines leaving one point, making four angles p, q, r and s that add up to 360 degrees. Right: two straight lines crossing; the two angles marked x are opposite each other, and the two angles marked y are opposite each other.

blocks.statement: [[angles-at-a-point|Angles at a point]] add up to $360^{\circ}$. Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$.
blocks.why: The angles round a point fill one full turn, and a straight line is half of that turn.

blocks.text: Two straight lines that cross make two pairs of [[vertically-opposite-angles|vertically opposite angles]].

blocks.why: In the figure, $x + y = 180^{\circ}$ along one line. The angle opposite $x$ also adds to $y$ to make $180^{\circ}$, along the other line, so it equals $x$.

blocks.question: $ABC$ is a straight line and $D$ is a point above it. Angle $ABD = 47^{\circ}$. Find angle $DBC$. Give a reason for your answer.
steps: Angles $ABD$ and $DBC$ sit side by side on the straight line $ABC$.
Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$, so angle $DBC = 180^{\circ} - 47^{\circ} = 133^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: Two straight lines cross at $X$. One angle at $X$ is $(3x + 10)^{\circ}$, and the angle vertically opposite it is $(5x - 34)^{\circ}$. Find the size of each of these two angles.
steps: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so $3x + 10 = 5x - 34$.
Take $3x$ from both sides and add $34$ to both sides: $44 = 2x$, so $x = 22$.
Each angle is $3 \times 22 + 10 = 76^{\circ}$. Check: $5 \times 22 - 34 = 76$.

blocks.prompt: Three angles meet at a point. They are $135^{\circ}$, $x^{\circ}$ and $2x^{\circ}$. Find $x$.
blocks.hint: Angles at a point add up to $360^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: Straight lines $PQ$ and $RS$ cross at $X$. Which reason shows that angle $PXR$ equals angle $QXS$?
blocks.hint: Are the two angles next to each other, or opposite each other?

options.text: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°
Angles at a point add up to 360°

blocks.explain: Angles $PXR$ and $QXS$ are opposite each other at the crossing, so they are vertically opposite.

blocks.text: Adding angles to $180^{\circ}$ when they only look as if they are on a straight line. Use the fact only when the question says the line is straight.
Tear the three corners off a paper triangle and put them side by side. They always make a straight line.

blocks.statement: The [[angle-sum|angle sum]] of a triangle is $180^{\circ}$. The angle sum of a [[quadrilateral|quadrilateral]] is $360^{\circ}$.
blocks.why: A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, and $2 \times 180^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$. If the shape has a dent, use the diagonal from the dent.

blocks.text: The $360^{\circ}$ is true for every quadrilateral, even one with a dent. At a dent the angle inside the shape is a [[reflex-angle|reflex angle]], more than $180^{\circ}$.
An [[isosceles-triangle|isosceles triangle]] has two equal sides. The two angles opposite them, the base angles, are equal.

blocks.question: Triangle $PQR$ has $PQ = PR$. $QRS$ is a straight line, and angle $PRS = 116^{\circ}$. Find angle $QPR$. Give a reason for each step.
steps: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$: angle $PRQ = 180^{\circ} - 116^{\circ} = 64^{\circ}$.
$PQ = PR$, so the triangle is isosceles with equal base angles at $Q$ and $R$: angle $PQR = 64^{\circ}$.
Angles in a triangle add up to $180^{\circ}$: angle $QPR = 180^{\circ} - 64^{\circ} - 64^{\circ} = 52^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is an arrowhead shape with a dent at $D$. Angle $DAB = 34^{\circ}$, angle $ABC = 51^{\circ}$ and angle $BCD = 29^{\circ}$. Find the reflex angle $ADC$.
steps: Angles in a quadrilateral add up to $360^{\circ}$, and the angle inside the shape at $D$ is reflex.
Reflex angle $ADC = 360^{\circ} - 34^{\circ} - 51^{\circ} - 29^{\circ} = 246^{\circ}$.
Check: $246$ is between $180$ and $360$, so the angle is reflex, as the dent needs.

blocks.prompt: The angles of a triangle are $x^{\circ}$, $(x + 20)^{\circ}$ and $(2x - 4)^{\circ}$. Find the largest angle, in degrees.
blocks.hint: Add the three angles and set the total equal to $180^{\circ}$.
blocks.explain: $4x + 16 = 180$, so $x = 41$. The angles are $41^{\circ}$, $61^{\circ}$ and $78^{\circ}$, so the largest is $78^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: Three angles of a quadrilateral are $72^{\circ}$, $95^{\circ}$ and $104^{\circ}$. Find the fourth angle, in degrees.
blocks.hint: A quadrilateral's angles add up to $360^{\circ}$.

blocks.text: Forgetting the second base angle of an isosceles triangle. When you know the top angle, the two base angles share what is left of the $180^{\circ}$, so halve it.
A line that crosses two [[parallel|parallel]] lines is called a transversal. It makes four angles at each crossing.
Because the lines are parallel, both crossings look exactly the same. The angles come in three kinds of pair.

blocks.alt: Three copies of two parallel lines, marked with arrows, crossed by a slanting line. Left, corresponding: the angle above each parallel line on the right of the slanting line is shaded; they are in the same position and are equal. Middle, alternate: the angle below the top line on the left and the angle above the bottom line on the right are shaded; they sit inside the pair of lines, one each side of the slanting line, and are equal. Right, co-interior: the angle below the top line on the left and the angle above the bottom line on the left are shaded; they sit inside the pair of lines, both on the left, and add up to 180 degrees.
blocks.caption: Arrows mark the parallel lines.

blocks.statement: [[corresponding-angles|Corresponding angles]] are equal. They are in the same position at each crossing, such as above the line and to the right of the transversal.
blocks.why: Slide the top crossing along the transversal and it lands exactly on the bottom one.

blocks.statement: [[alternate-angles|Alternate angles]] are equal. They are inside the pair of lines, one each side of the transversal, making a Z shape.
blocks.why: Each one is vertically opposite an angle that corresponds to the other.

blocks.statement: [[co-interior-angles|Co-interior angles]] add up to $180^{\circ}$: they are supplementary. They are inside the pair of lines, both on one side of the transversal.
blocks.why: One of them is alternate to the angle next to the other, and those two neighbours make a straight line, $180^{\circ}$.

blocks.alt: Two horizontal parallel lines marked with arrows: AB on top, with A on the left and B on the right, and CD below, with C on the left and D on the right. A slanting straight line EF goes from E, above and to the right, down to F, below and to the left. It crosses AB at G and CD at H. Not to scale.
blocks.caption: Use this figure for the examples and checks below.

blocks.question: In the figure, angle $EGB = 57^{\circ}$. Find angle $CHG$. Give a reason for each step.
steps: Angles $EGB$ and $GHD$ are both above their line and to the right of $EF$. Corresponding angles are equal, so angle $GHD = 57^{\circ}$.
Angles $CHG$ and $GHD$ lie on the straight line $CD$. Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$, so angle $CHG = 180^{\circ} - 57^{\circ} = 123^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: In the figure, angle $AGH = (2y + 7)^{\circ}$ and angle $CHG = (3y + 18)^{\circ}$. Find angle $CHG$. Give a reason for your working.
steps: Angles $AGH$ and $CHG$ lie between the parallel lines, both to the left of $EF$. Co-interior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
Take $25$ from both sides: $5y = 155$, so $y = 31$.
Angle $CHG = 3 \times 31 + 18 = 111^{\circ}$. Check: angle $AGH = 69$, and $69 + 111 = 180$.

blocks.prompt: In the figure, which pair are alternate angles?
blocks.hint: Alternate angles are inside the pair of lines, one each side of $EF$.
blocks.explain: Angle $AGH$ is below $AB$ on the left of $EF$. Angle $GHD$ is above $CD$ on the right. They form a Z, so they are alternate.

blocks.prompt: In the figure, angle $AGE = 118^{\circ}$. Find angle $GHD$, in degrees.
blocks.explain: Angle $EGB = 180 - 118 = 62^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line). Angle $GHD$ corresponds to angle $EGB$, so it is $62^{\circ}$ too.

blocks.text: Calling two angles alternate when both are on one side of the transversal. Matching positions means corresponding; both inside the lines on one side means co-interior.
A [[regular-polygon|regular polygon]] has all its sides equal and all its angles equal. Its [[interior-angle|interior angles]] are the angles inside the shape.
Extend one side past a vertex. The angle between the extension and the next side is an [[exterior-angle|exterior angle]].

blocks.alt: Two diagrams. Left: a pentagon with two dashed lines from its top corner to the two far corners, splitting it into 3 triangles, so its angles add up to 3 times 180, which is 540 degrees. Right: a regular hexagon with each side extended past the next corner by a dashed line. At the top corner, the exterior angle e between the extended side and the next side is marked, next to the interior angle i inside the hexagon. The six exterior angles add up to 360 degrees, and i plus e is 180 degrees.

blocks.text: Walk all the way round a polygon. At each corner you turn through the exterior angle. After one lap you face the way you started, so you have turned $360^{\circ}$.

blocks.statement: The exterior angles of a regular polygon with $n$ sides add up to $360^{\circ}$, so each one is $\frac{360^{\circ}}{n}$. At each vertex, the interior and exterior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
blocks.why: You turn one full lap, and the interior and exterior angles at a vertex lie on a straight line.

blocks.statement: The interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides add up to $(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$.
blocks.why: In a polygon with no reflex angle, lines from one vertex split it into $n - 2$ triangles. The pentagon in the figure has $5$ sides and $3$ triangles: $3 \times 180^{\circ} = 540^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: Find the size of each interior angle of a regular octagon.
steps: An octagon has $8$ sides. Each exterior angle is $360^{\circ} \div 8 = 45^{\circ}$.
Interior and exterior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$, so each interior angle is $180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ} = 135^{\circ}$.
Check with the angle sum: $(8 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 1080^{\circ}$, and $1080 \div 8 = 135$.

blocks.question: A regular polygon has interior angles of $162^{\circ}$ each. How many sides does it have?
steps: Each exterior angle is $180^{\circ} - 162^{\circ} = 18^{\circ}$.
The exterior angles add up to $360^{\circ}$, so the number of sides is $n = 360 \div 18 = 20$.

blocks.prompt: Find the size of each interior angle of a regular hexagon.
blocks.hint: Find the exterior angle first: a hexagon has $6$ sides.

blocks.prompt: Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is $20^{\circ}$. How many sides does it have?
blocks.hint: The exterior angles add up to $360^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: Could a regular polygon have interior angles of $100^{\circ}$?
blocks.hint: Work out the exterior angle, then the number of sides.

options.text: No, because 360 ÷ 80 is not a whole number

blocks.explain: The exterior angle would be $80^{\circ}$, and $360 \div 80 = 4.5$. A polygon cannot have $4.5$ sides, so no.

verify.truth: No, because 360 ÷ 80 is not a whole number

blocks.text: Dividing $360$ by the interior angle. Only the exterior angles add up to $360^{\circ}$, so find the exterior angle first.
The interior angle sum $(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$ works for every polygon, regular or irregular, even one with a reflex angle. In an irregular polygon the angles differ, so work with the total.

blocks.statement: If no interior angle is reflex, the exterior angles of any polygon add up to $360^{\circ}$.
blocks.why: Walking round the shape, you still turn through one full lap.

blocks.question: The angles of a pentagon are $2x^{\circ}$, $2x^{\circ}$, $(x + 40)^{\circ}$, $110^{\circ}$ and $125^{\circ}$. Find $x$.
steps: A pentagon has $5$ sides, so its angle sum is $(5 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 540^{\circ}$.
Take $275$ from both sides: $5x = 265$, so $x = 53$.
Check: the angles are $106$, $106$, $93$, $110$ and $125$, which add up to $540$.

blocks.question: A hexagon has no reflex angles. Five of its exterior angles are $40^{\circ}$, $75^{\circ}$, $50^{\circ}$, $65^{\circ}$ and $72^{\circ}$. Find the interior angle at the sixth vertex.
steps: The exterior angles add up to $360^{\circ}$: the sixth is $360^{\circ} - (40^{\circ} + 75^{\circ} + 50^{\circ} + 65^{\circ} + 72^{\circ}) = 360^{\circ} - 302^{\circ} = 58^{\circ}$.
Interior and exterior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$: the interior angle is $180^{\circ} - 58^{\circ} = 122^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: Seven of the angles of an irregular octagon add up to $975^{\circ}$. Find the eighth angle, in degrees.
blocks.hint: An octagon has $8$ sides. Find its angle sum first.
blocks.explain: The angle sum is $(8 - 2) \times 180 = 1080^{\circ}$, so the eighth angle is $1080 - 975 = 105^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: The interior angles of a polygon add up to $1260^{\circ}$. How many sides does it have?

blocks.text: Using $360^{\circ}$ as the total of the interior angles. $360^{\circ}$ is the exterior total; the interior total is $(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$.
Angles at a point add up to $360^{\circ}$. Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$.
Vertically opposite angles are equal.
Angle sum: triangle $180^{\circ}$, quadrilateral $360^{\circ}$.
Parallel lines: corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, co-interior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$.
Regular polygon with $n$ sides: exterior angle $= \frac{360^{\circ}}{n}$, and interior angle $= 180^{\circ} -$ exterior angle.
Interior angles of a polygon with $n$ sides add up to $(n - 2) \times 180^{\circ}$.
Exterior angles of any polygon with no reflex angle add up to $360^{\circ}$.

mistakes: Giving the exterior angle when the question asks for the interior angle. Reread which one is asked for; the interior angle is $180^{\circ}$ minus the exterior angle.
Writing "Z angles", "F angles" or "alternative angles" as a reason. Use the names alternate, corresponding and co-interior.
Using an angle drawn outside a shape as one of its interior angles. At a dent the interior angle is reflex: $360^{\circ}$ minus the angle outside.
Stopping at an angle found on the way. Reread the three letters of the angle asked for before you write the answer.
examTips: "Give a reason" or "give a geometrical reason": write the fact in full, such as "co-interior angles add up to $180^{\circ}$". The value alone usually earns only part of the marks.
Diagrams marked NOT TO SCALE must not be measured. Work out every angle from a named fact.
Write each angle on the diagram as you find it, and name it with three letters in your working, such as angle $PQR$.
